claim: NVIDIA's cuDNN DSA kernels are Hopper/Blackwell-only: most kernels target SM90 and SM100+, and Sparse Attention Backward, Score Recompute, Indexer Forward, Indexer Top-K and Indexer Backward all require SM90 or SM100, with the combined compressed-logits+Top-K forward SM100-only.
stance_target: The feasibility of using NVIDIA's DSA training kernels on a CMP 170HX (GA100 / SM80) box
scope_conditions: cuDNN Frontend v1.28.0, experimental API; DSA module limitations section
quoted_support: Most kernels target Hopper (SM90) and Blackwell (SM100+) GPUs. ... Architecture support - Sparse Attention Backward, Score Recompute, Indexer Forward, Indexer Top-K, and Indexer Backward support SM90 and SM100. The combined compressed-logits + Top-K forward is SM100-only; the standalone Indexer Top-K remains SM90+.

claim: The only DSA path usable on pre-Hopper hardware is the pure-PyTorch reference implementation (test/python/fe_api/dsa/dsa_reference.py::ref_sparse_attention_forward), because the production sparse-attention forward kernel is FlashMLA in C++ and is not integrated into this module.
stance_target: What a CSA2 reproduction on Ampere-class cards must implement itself
quoted_support: The production sparse-attention forward kernel (FlashMLA) is C++ and is not integrated here; when evaluating the backward, use the pure-PyTorch reference in test/python/fe_api/dsa/dsa_reference.py::ref_sparse_attention_forward.

claim: The module documents an explicit training-score loss path in which attn_score and index_score feed IndexerBackward to produce d_index_q, d_weights and d_index_k — confirming that the indexer is trained by a distillation-style loss against main attention rather than end-to-end through the non-differentiable top-k.
stance_target: The repo's claim that top-k selection is non-differentiable and the indexer needs a separate distillation loss
quoted_support: Training-score loss path: attn_score, index_score --> IndexerBackward --> d_index_q, d_weights, d_index_k (SparseIndexer/AttnScoreRecompute and DenseIndexer/AttnScoreRecompute produce these score tensors; DenseIndexerBackward consumes dense raw scores.)

claim: Indexer Backward is a three-stage pipeline: an in-place score-grad precompute from attn_score (target) and index_score (predict), three warp-specialised GEMMs producing d_index_q, d_weights and a dIndexK_f32 accumulator, then a pure-torch dtype cast.
stance_target: The implementation complexity of the indexer training loss
quoted_support: Three-stage sparse top-K pipeline that produces the training gradients for the indexer tower: 1. ScoreGradSm90 / ScoreGradSm100 (kernel 1) - in-place score-grad precompute from attn_score (target) and index_score (predict). 2. IndexerBackwardSm90 / IndexerBackwardSm100 (kernel 2) - three warp-specialised GEMMs produce d_index_q, d_weights, and a dIndexK_f32 accumulator. 3. Pure-torch dtype cast (kernel 3) converts dIndexK_f32 to the output dtype.

claim: The DSA indexer requires head_dim == 128 and H_kv == 1 (multi-query attention), with qhead_per_kv_head in {16,32,64} on SM90 and {32,64} on SM100 — so a scaled-down CSA2 reproduction must keep the indexer's head geometry fixed at 128.
stance_target: How freely a small CSA2 variant can be reshaped
quoted_support: Constraints - head_dim == 128. The SM90 direct path supports qhead_per_kv_head in {16, 32, 64} and currently requires H_kv == 1; SM100 BF16 dense and combined Top-K paths support qhead_per_kv_head in {32, 64}, as do their MXFP8 paths. All currently require H_kv == 1 (MQA).

claim: The standalone radix Indexer Top-K kernel supports top_k <= 2048 and SM90+, which is consistent with the 512-1024 top-k values used by V4-class models and with the 16,384-candidate hierarchical pool being a separate selection stage.
stance_target: The repo's stated 512 top-k and 16,384 candidate pool
quoted_support: Radix top-K kernel for selecting candidate KV indices from indexer scores, with variable per-row effective length. ... Constraints - SM90+, top_k <= 2048

claim: FP8 and MXFP8 indexer backward are not supported: the backward wrapper requires BF16 Q/K/W inputs, so low-precision indexer training is forward-only in this module.
stance_target: Whether a low-precision (FP8/FP4) indexer can be trained with these kernels
quoted_support: FP8 and MXFP8 indexer backward are not currently supported because the backward wrapper requires BF16 Q/K/W inputs.

claim: The module is request-or-fail rather than silently falling back: the TileLang fallback present in the upstream repo is dropped, and if the CuTe-DSL path fails the wrapper raises RuntimeError.
stance_target: How a failed DSA kernel launch behaves in a training loop
quoted_support: The TileLang fallback present in the upstream repo is dropped here (CuTe-DSL only). If the CuTe-DSL path fails the wrapper raises RuntimeError rather than silently falling back.

claim: The API is explicitly experimental and subject to change, and the SM100 sparse backward v2 backend is opt-in with a narrow envelope (SM100 only, H=64, D=128, block_I=128, topk a multiple of 128 in [128,2048]).
stance_target: The stability risk of building a training pipeline on these kernels
scope_conditions: Module header and Section 8 SM100 sparse backward v2 envelope
quoted_support: This is an experimental API and subject to change. ... Envelope (validated by check_support when a plan is created, and re-validated against the real tensors on every execute - cache hits included - before any buffer is mutated) - SM100 (10, 0) only; H == 64, D == 128, block_I == 128; topk % 128 == 0 with 128 <= topk <= 2048
